title: Probative scan and stub strategy for Responses compatibility
creator: Aisha Martinez
description: Run a probative scan of feature-level mismatches between the OpenAI Responses API and Redwood's runtime semantics, then produce a minimal runtime stub/adapter strategy to bridge high-risk gaps. This ticket captures the discovery work, mapping catalog, and a lightweight shim prototype plan that preserves predictable latency and enables gradual rollout. Focus areas: streaming event line semantics (delta vs final), tool/function calling lifecycle (invoke/accept/complete/error), structured output schemas (types, validation, partial structures), and observability/telemetry to quantify lossiness. Deliverables: compatibility catalog, lossiness heuristics, shim interface design, contract tests, and canary rollout plan for the stub adapter.
acceptance_criteria: Comprehensive compatibility catalog mapping at least 28 discrete OpenAI Responses features to Redwood runtime equivalents or documented divergences
Lossiness heuristic defined with a loss_score metric and test harness that produces reproducible discrepancy reports for 100 canonical prompts
Shim prototype implemented that translates streaming events and function call lifecycle for one model family and passes integration tests in local canary environment
Canary rollout plan with fallbacks and telemetry dashboards documented and reviewed by SRE and Product
Security review required flag set and KMS/HSM considerations documented for tool call payloads
tasks: Inventory OpenAI Responses event types and payload schemas
Map each event to Redwood internal event model (identify one-to-many and many-to-one mappings)
Define lossiness heuristics and scoring algorithm (token-level, field-level, semantic mismatch)
Implement streaming translator for chunk/delta/final events (Node runtime prototype)
Prototype tool/function call lifecycle mapping including ephemeral context and tool-result reconciliation
Create contract test suite with 100 canonical prompts and expected translated traces
Add telemetry: mismatch_rate, loss_score, tool_invoke_fail_rate, latency_delta
Draft canary rollout policy (percent, geos, model-families) and automatic rollback criteria
Write runbook for common mismatch classes and mitigation steps

notes: Probe rationale: previous migrations failed when tool-call order semantics diverged; early detection reduces incident scope.

Strategy: implement a minimal deterministic translator rather than full behavioral parity. For irreconcilable differences expose a visible degradation mode with clear telemetry so PMs can communicate to customers.

Fallbacks: 1) Route traffic to Redwood-hosted simpler completions model with tool emulation; 2) Return a structured failure response that includes a recommended user action; 3) Auto-failover to previous stable runtime version.
Test coverage: contract tests must include injection of out-of-order events, truncated deltas, duplicate tool-result events, and simulated network reordering.
